items.title: The cosk_0 fibre product of a surjection is a trivial Kan fibration
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file simplicial.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-cosk-minus-one-equivalence at source lines 6367-6378: for a surjection f : A to B, the simplicial set whose n-simplices are the (n+1)-fold fibre products of A over B maps to the constant simplicial set B by a trivial Kan fibration. The proof at source lines 6380-6391 observes that this simplicial set fits into a cartesian square over the square of the constant simplicial sets cosk_0(A) and cosk_0(B), that the right vertical arrow is a trivial Kan fibration because f is surjective, and concludes by base change of trivial Kan fibrations. It is short; the substance is recognising the fibre-product description as a pullback and knowing that trivial Kan fibrations are stable under base change.
